item: The restore-hold 503 sends a Retry-After made from the live file's size, or none when no figure is true
summary: A save refused at once during a restore's hold (its thread holds the single-writer gate) now sends Retry-After = ceil(1 s + 0.5 s per GiB of the live file read when the hold started); one refused after the full KV_WRITE_WAIT_S wait sends none, as does a stuck lock. The old constant 30 was the save's own wait, not a measurement. Base and rate from the 2026-10-17 restore-hold measurement (hold 0.04 to 1.95 s up to 1 GB, os.replace about 0.5 s per GiB, ext4 virtual disk); above 1 GiB, on Windows, with a large -wal and on a real store it is inferred or unmeasured and the code says so. No client reads the header on a 503, so nothing a user sees changes. Real SIGALRM interrupts on hold_writes(0): 0 of 128,429 left the hold set.
